case_title: Rajndawar v. High Court of Delhi
statutory_provisions: Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 s.2(c) read with ss.10 and 15; Constitution of India Art.215
evidence_type: Complainant's unilateral allegations; Bar Council order dated 30.09.2006; affidavit filed by the accused
mitigating_circumstances: Accused complied with the direction to refund the money; Disciplinary Authority completely absolved the accused
trial_court_outcome: Not applicable: the Additional Sessions Judge made a reference to the High Court and did not decide guilt; no sentence imposed at that level
high_court_outcome: Accused held guilty of criminal contempt; fine of Rs. 2,000 under the Contempt of Courts Act and suspension from practice for two months under Article 215
neutral_facts: The victim was facing trial in a separate criminal case and had engaged the accused, an advocate, to defend him in that matter. The victim later complained that the accused had charged professional fees of about Rs. 7.05 lakh, had provided no active assistance in the case, and had withdrawn from representing him. The victim sought a refund of at least Rs. 6 lakh. The accused maintained that appropriate fees had been charged for professional services actually rendered, and that the sums received were not for any other purpose. The Bar Council of Delhi examined the complaint. Its findings were that the accused had withdrawn from the engagement without sufficient cause and had not refunded the unearned part of the fee, but that the matter did not involve misconduct such as misrepresentation, deliberate receipt of money by falsification or false assurances. The victim did not seek disciplinary action and confined the prayer to a refund. The Bar Council held that a refund of Rs. 4 lakh was justified, with no interest payable.
number_of_offences: 1 charged (criminal contempt under s.2(c) read with ss.10 and 15); 0 finally upheld
financial_property_loss: Complainant alleged fees of Rs. 7.05 lakh were charged; refund of Rs. 6 lakh sought; Bar Council ordered refund of Rs. 4 lakh, which the accused complied with
motive: alleged: dispute over fees charged and the accused's withdrawal from the case
key_evidence_accepted: None accepted as proof of guilt; the court relied on the Bar Council order absolving the accused of misconduct and on the non-compliance with procedural safeguards
post_offence_conduct: Complied with the direction to refund money
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 02.01.2007; Supreme Court: 26.07.2017
legal_representation: Accused (appellant): K. V. Vishwanathan, Sr. Adv., with Ashok Mathur, Ms. Nidhi Agrawal, Sameer Dawar, Dhananjay Ray, Advs. Respondent: C. K. Sucharita, Adv. (no State counsel named)
investigation_status: Complaint examined by the Bar Council of Delhi; order dated 30.09.2006
procedural_irregularity: Accused was not given an opportunity to adduce evidence or cross-examine the complainant; procedural safeguards were not followed
appeal_history: Trial court (Additional Sessions Judge): made reference to High Court, no decision on guilt. High Court: guilty of criminal contempt; fine Rs. 2,000 and two-month suspension. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, conviction and sentence set aside
defence_argument: Conviction rested on the complainant's unilateral version; the accused was not allowed to adduce evidence or cross-examine the complainant; appropriate fees were charged for services rendered
legal_principle_applied: In contempt proceedings the contemnor must be given an opportunity to establish innocence; conviction cannot rest solely on unproved allegations
judicial_mitigating_factors: Accused had complied with the refund direction; disciplinary authority completely absolved the accused; procedural safeguards not followed
